question: UNRWA – 10 % of workers linked to Hamas

According to US media reports, 10 % of UNRWA’s 12 000 employees are directly or indirectly collaborating with the terrorist organisation Hamas. This means that a large number of UNRWA staff were involved in the terrible terrorist attacks carried out on Israel on 7 October 2023, which resulted in more than 1 200 deaths and hundreds of kidnappings. In light of the above, it is uncertain how the Commission intends to continue providing further financial support to UNRWA using Union taxpayers’ money. 1.
What action does the Commission intend to take beyond the measures announced by Commissioner Várhelyi on 29 January 2024, when talk was only of 12 staff members?
If the Commission learns the names of the 1 200 accused persons, what direct action does it intend to take to prevent them from being paid with EU taxpayers’ money?

Given the structural problems faced by UNRWA and the large-scale employment of members of a terrorist organisation, does the Commission consider it necessary to call for a change of mandate and thus a change in the tasks entrusted to UNRWA, or even to permanently reassign parts of the funding allocated to UNRWA to other organisations?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.7.2024) The EU has expressed grave concern with regards to the very serious allegations made on 24 January 2024 against 12 staff of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). The Commission has engaged with UNRWA’s Commissioner-General and welcomed his commitment to tackle the serious issues at stake.
Letters outlining the way forward with all the measures and procedures for the Commission’s conditional funding for UNRWA were exchanged on 1 and 6 March 2024.

The conditions for the disbursement of the first tranche were the following: agreement by UNRWA on the three workstreams (the screening of UNRWA staff; system audit; reinforcement of the Department of Internal Investigations and Ethics office) and the signature of the EU-UNRWA contribution agreement; declaration in writing by UNRWA that up-todate, necessary and proportionate information on staff has been shared and will be done on a quarterly basis; and the adoption by UNRWA of a concept note detailing how to strengthen Department of Internal Oversight Services (DIOS), including the establishment of a new neutrality investigation unit and ethics office1.

Disbursement of the second tranche was conditional on the following: the Agency ensures the screening and vetting system against relevant EU sanctions list in place; UNRWA provides a progress report on the state of implementation of the concept note on how to strengthen DIOS and ethics departments; an action plan is adopted by UNRWA to implement the recommendations of the United Nations independent review.

Following UNRWA’s fulfilment of the above conditions, the Commission processed the first tranche of EUR 50 million on 7 March 2024, and the second tranche of EUR 16 million on 31 May 2024, respectively, out of the EUR 82 million for UNRWA in 2024.
Disbursement of the third tranche of EUR 16 million is subject to the implementation of the agreement with UNRWA and the Agency’s compliance with the agreed conditions and milestones.
